name: Osteoporosis
definition: Systemic skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone strength and increased fragility-fracture risk. It is often silent until fracture.

typical: Fragility vertebral, hip or wrist fracture
Height loss or kyphosis after vertebral fractures

redFlags.item: Acute suspected hip or vertebral fracture
Features of malignancy, myeloma or severe secondary metabolic disease

investigations.principle: Use fracture history, DXA and clinical risk assessment together.
investigations.MRI: MRI is not routine for osteoporosis itself; useful for acute vertebral-fracture characterization.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs are useful for vertebral-fracture assessment when indicated.

green: Adequate nutrition, protein, calcium and vitamin D sufficiency
Progressive resistance, balance and weight-bearing exercise appropriate to fracture risk
amber: Anti-fracture pharmacotherapy is individualized according to fracture risk, renal function, prior fracture and guideline criteria.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Asthi-dhatu-kshaya phenotype may be explored as a correlation but does not replace DXA/fracture-risk diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Systemic skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone strength and increased fragility-fracture risk. It is often silent until fracture.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.

sources.title: Clinical guideline for prevention and treatment of osteoporosis — updated Dec 2024
